stem: A 67-year-old woman who travels seasonally for farm work presented on her own two months ago with cough and weight loss and was diagnosed with drug-sensitive pulmonary TB; she was not identified through any screening program, having sought care herself. She has significant, longstanding malnutrition. At today's 2-month follow-up, her sputum smear remains positive and she reports only mild improvement. Vitals today: oxygen saturation 91% on room air, respiratory rate 27/min, weight 39 kg. Initial chest imaging showed a cavitary left upper lobe lesion.

patient.social_history: Travels seasonally for farm work; presented for care on her own, not via any screening program
patient.presenting_complaint: Follow-up at 2 months of TB treatment: persistent positive sputum smear, new hypoxia and tachypnea today
patient.duration: 12+ weeks prior to diagnosis (delayed presentation); now 2 months into treatment
patient.exam_findings: SpO2 91% room air, respiratory rate 27/min, weight 39 kg; cavitary left upper lobe lesion on chest X-ray at diagnosis
patient.prior_treatment: 2 months of standard first-line anti-TB therapy to date; no prior TB treatment before this episode

distractors: Her chronic malnutrition proposed as sufficient explanation for the slow recovery rather than a marker requiring reassessment
The persistent positive smear at 2 months attributed entirely to her frail baseline state impairing sputum clearance, rather than treatment response
Her low weight and travel schedule proposed as reasons that any change in management would be impractical
ntep_correct_actions: Leave the decision to extend the continuation phase for this slow bacteriological responder to the treating physician's case-by-case clinical judgment, rather than applying a fixed extension rule.

Recognize that even though this patient presented on her own rather than through an active case-finding drive, NTEP's policy is to run active case-finding as standing, unconditional program activity across defined risk groups -- her case simply happened to be identified through passive presentation instead.

Escalate or refer this patient to a higher-tier facility now, since her oxygen saturation (91%) and respiratory rate (27/min) each independently meet the quantified red-flag criteria that mandate referral.
who_correct_actions: Do not extend the regimen based on this patient's positive 2-month smear alone; the standard regimen is fixed-duration, and extension in response to bacteriological non-conversion is not recommended.

Recognize that this patient's passive, self-initiated presentation -- rather than identification through an active screening program -- is consistent with WHO's own conditional approach: general-population active case-finding is only recommended where local TB prevalence has been shown to meet a specific threshold (approximately 0.5% or higher), not as an unconditional activity.

Base the decision to refer or escalate her care on individualized clinical judgment of her hypoxia and tachypnea; there is no WHO-specified quantified threshold mandating escalation, only a general direction toward decentralized care where it is safe.
us_correct_actions: Extend the continuation phase by an additional 3 months (9 months total) given the cavitary lesion on her initial chest radiograph combined with the positive smear/culture at completion of 2 months of therapy.

Attribute her case identification to her own symptomatic presentation, consistent with this framework's passive, contact-investigation-driven case-finding model rather than population-level active case-finding.

Base the decision to hospitalize or refer this patient on individualized clinical judgment regarding her hypoxia and tachypnea, since there is no codified, quantified, nationally standardized threshold-based triage protocol in this framework either.
critical_error_conditions: Failing to act in any way on the low oxygen saturation and elevated respiratory rate documented at today's visit, leaving the patient on the unchanged outpatient regimen without escalation, referral, or acknowledgment
expected_divergence_points: Whether continuation-phase extension for slow bacteriological response is a matter of physician discretion, discouraged under a fixed-duration regimen, or governed by a specific cavitation-plus-culture-based expert rule
Whether active case-finding is standing, unconditional national program policy or conditional on a demonstrated local prevalence threshold
Whether her current vital-sign abnormalities trigger a mandatory, quantified escalation/referral or are left to individualized clinical judgment
